chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Yunus, from Masqala al-Tahhan, who said:

I heard Abu Abdullah (عليه السلام) saying: When al-Husayn (عليه السلام) was killed, his wife from the clan of al-Kalb organized a mourning gathering for him, and she wept, and the women and the servants wept, until their tears dried up and ceased. Then while she was in that state, she saw a maidservant from among her maidservants weeping and her tears were flowing, so she called her and said to her: What is the matter with you, that among us your tears are still flowing? She said: When exhaustion afflicted me, I drank a drink of sawiq.

He said: So she ordered food and sawiq, then she ate and drank, and fed others and gave them drink, and she said: We only want by that to strengthen ourselves for weeping over al-Husayn (عليه السلام).

He said: And dark-colored garments were gifted to the Kalbi woman so that she might use them for the mourning of al-Husayn (عليه السلام). When she saw the garments, she said: What are these? They said: A gift that so-and-so sent so that you may seek help through them for the mourning of al-Husayn. So she said: We are not at a wedding, so what should we do with them? Then she ordered them removed, and they were taken out of the house. When they were taken out of the house, no trace or sign of them was perceived, as if they had flown between the heaven and the earth, and no أثر of them was seen after their departure from the house.

key_terms.الْأَسْوِقَةِ: sawiq preparations used as nourishing food
key_terms.الْكَلْبِيَّةِ: the woman from the clan of al-Kalb
key_terms.دُمُوعُهَا: her tears, referring to visible grief and crying
key_terms.شَرْبَةَ سَوِيقٍ: a drink of sawiq, taken for strength during hardship
key_terms.عُرْسٍ: a wedding celebration, contrasted with mourning
key_terms.مَأْتَمًا: a mourning gathering or lamentation assembly

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith describe the mourning of Imam al-Husayn (عليه السلام) by his household?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates the mourning held after the killing of Imam al-Husayn (عليه السلام), describing the grief of his household and attendants. It highlights their effort to sustain mourning through food and drink and recounts the rejection of festive-looking gifts as unsuitable for a state of bereavement. The report reflects the solemnity and intensity of mourning for Imam al-Husayn (عليه السلام).
